Test Steps: 1) In Forge test world install `AG_ashen-gate-utilities_v0.2.0_Alpha.zip` via supported module-folder upload. 2) Enable Ashen Gate | Utilities under Game Settings > Manage Modules. 3) Reload. 4) Open Actors > Utilities.
Expected Outcome: Single Utilities launcher and functional window show v0.2.0 Alpha, with no startup console errors.

Test Steps: 1) Keep Utilities Player Access disabled (default). 2) Log in using a separate player browser. 3) Confirm Actors launcher absent. 4) Press F12 > Console and run `await game.modules.get('ashen-gate-utilities').api.open().then(() => 'UNEXPECTED OPEN', e => e.message)`.
Expected Outcome: No launcher; console returns a message saying Utilities access is hidden by the GM. No GM data is shown.

Test Steps: 1) GM opens Actors > Utilities > GM Setup. 2) Check Enable Player Access. 3) Click Save Player Access. 4) On already-connected player browser inspect Actors > Utilities and click it.
Expected Outcome: Player launcher appears without needing a new login and opens a view without GM Setup or History.

Test Steps: 1) With Player Access enabled, open player Console (F12). 2) Run `await game.modules.get('ashen-gate-utilities').api.playerAccess.setEnabled(false).then(() => 'UNEXPECTED WRITE', e => e.message)`. 3) Try to find GM Setup in tabs.
Expected Outcome: Console returns `GM only.` and GM Setup/GM-only buttons remain inaccessible. No access setting changes.

Test Steps: 1) Enable General Manager and Utilities, open Utilities from Actors. 2) Disable General Manager in Manage Modules; reload. 3) Open Utilities again, navigate every tab.
Expected Outcome: Utilities functions without Manager; fallback styling is readable; no changes to stored sessions.

Test Steps: 1) Enable two or more AG player modules with player visibility. 2) Open Actors sidebar. 3) Check Utilities launch button size/order and hover focus. 4) Refresh sidebar and verify only one Utilities button.
Expected Outcome: One full-width 36px-high Utilities button in shared Actors group ordered rank 60, 5px spacing, without duplicate controls.

Test Steps: 1) GM, disposable Forge world with Utilities v0.2.0 enabled and at least one non-GM user: press F12, open Console, paste and run `await (await import('/modules/ashen-gate-utilities/fixtures/setup.mjs')).setup()`. 2) Open Actors directory and Roll Tables directory; verify two test character Actors, two tables, and one Item are present. 3) Open each Actor sheet and check owner assignment.
Expected Outcome: Real native documents are created, visibly prefixed `AG TEST |`, with first two player users assigned ownership where available; rerun does not duplicate.

Test Steps: 1) Run UTL-07. 2) GM opens Utilities > Group Checks. 3) Title `Test Crossing`; check the two AG TEST characters. 4) Set DC 15, 2 rolls per character, permitted Athletics/Acrobatics/Perception. 5) Click Start Group Check. 6) Players look for an incoming Utilities window/prompt.
Expected Outcome: Four pending contribution slots; players see a prompt/auto-opened Group Checks view with a prominent Roll Now action; GM remains on the Group Check tab.

Test Steps: 1) With UTL-08 active, owner of `AG TEST | Bridge Scout` opens Group Checks. 2) Select Athletics and click Roll Now. 3) Resolve native dnd5e roll; review Chat and GM Group Checks.
Expected Outcome: Native ChatMessage roll evidence and a submission message are created. Connected GM accepts one contribution; progress reflects it once.

Test Steps: 1) Following UTL-09, attempt Athletics for Bridge Scout again. 2) Use Acrobatics for Bridge Scout instead. 3) Use Athletics for Field Warden on second player. 4) On first player, try to submit the unowned character.
Expected Outcome: Same character cannot repeat Athletics in the check; distinct skill succeeds, different character can use Athletics, and unowned character is not selectable.

Test Steps: 1) During an active partially submitted Group Check open GM Group Checks. 2) Click End & Record and confirm. 3) Open History. 4) Switch back to Group Checks.
Expected Outcome: Pending contributions are logged as Skipped; History records roller, skill, total, average and success/failure or No Result. No active Group Check remains.

Test Steps: 1) Complete UTL-11. 2) Open Group Checks. 3) Select both AG TEST characters; set DC 12 and one roll per character. 4) Click Start Group Check.
Expected Outcome: Fresh check accepts valid character selection without `Choose 1 to 24 characters` error. Prior History remains intact.

Test Steps: 1) With a Group Check active, click Roll Requests (both GM/player). 2) Observe view and attempt to create a Roll Request. 3) Return to Group Checks.
Expected Outcome: Roll Requests does not show the Group Check as its own active request. It explains another interaction is active and prevents accidental overwrite.

Test Steps: 1) In Group Checks with any active disposable check, click Cancel Session. 2) Confirm. 3) Open History, then Group Checks again.
Expected Outcome: Cancelled entry appears once in History; active slot clears, next interaction can begin.

Test Steps: 1) Start Group Check DC 15 with one contribution per AG TEST Actor. 2) Click Skip One for each character, confirming both. 3) Open History.
Expected Outcome: Result is No Result; both skips audited; active slot cleared.

Test Steps: 1) Start Group Check DC 15, two characters, one roll each. 2) Have players roll natively; compare accepted totals. 3) Use End & Record if slots remain. 4) Review GM History average and result.
Expected Outcome: Running/final average uses accepted totals only; UI displays one decimal but success compares the unrounded average. Skips never count as zero.

Test Steps: 1) Ensure no session is active. 2) GM opens Roll Requests, selects both AG TEST characters, chooses Perception and DC 15. 3) Click Send Roll Request. 4) Each owner uses Roll Now.
Expected Outcome: Separate Roll Request view shows one public native skill roll per Actor, not an averaged group outcome; each result is accepted once and archives on completion.

Test Steps: 1) Complete UTL-17. 2) GM opens History. 3) Read each Actor's result, skill and DC comparison.
Expected Outcome: Each participant is labeled Success or Failure versus DC 15, with roll total and skill, without a Group Check average.

Test Steps: 1) Start fresh one-slot Group Check. 2) Player submits one Roll Now. 3) Try to resubmit the same native proof via the normal UI if a pending slot remains; repeat rapid clicking. 4) GM checks History and progress.
Expected Outcome: One native ChatMessage proof cannot count twice; a completed check stays closed. Report any duplicate or unverified roll as FAIL.

Test Steps: 1) Start a two-Actor Group Check. 2) First player rolls. 3) Second player disconnects and reconnects with browser reload. 4) Second player opens Utilities and rolls.
Expected Outcome: Active session persists; accepted first result is not lost or duplicated; second character can finish normally.

Test Steps: 1) Run UTL-07. 2) GM opens Utilities > Roll Tables; choose `AG TEST | Crossing Reports`. 3) Click Roll Privately, edit the outgoing text. 4) Check only Player 1 and click Send Message. 5) Check Player 2's chat.
Expected Outcome: GM preview is editable; only Player 1 and GM see the outgoing whisper, Player 2 does not.

Test Steps: 1) GM Roll Tables > Crossing Reports. 2) Check Player 1, enable Auto-Send, then click Roll Privately. 3) Compare all three chat views.
Expected Outcome: One safe text message is delivered to selected Player 1 plus GM, not to Player 2.

Test Steps: 1) GM Roll Tables > `AG TEST | Unsafe Document Result`. 2) Click Roll Privately. 3) Observe UI and Chat.
Expected Outcome: Clear error states this RollTable contains document/compendium results. No Foundry popup/roll occurs and no protected source data is sent.

Test Steps: 1) GM opens Utilities > Conditions, selects `AG TEST | Bridge Scout`, chooses Poisoned and clicks Apply. 2) On player browser open Conditions. 3) Inspect native sheet/token and dashboard. 4) GM clicks Remove.
Expected Outcome: Native status appears and disappears without manual Utilities refresh on connected clients; player sees permitted status but cannot change it.

Test Steps: 1) With UTL-07 test Actors, GM opens Conditions. 2) Apply Poisoned to Bridge Scout and another standard condition to Field Warden. 3) Inspect both panes and icons. 4) Player opens Conditions.
Expected Outcome: GM sees both party characters and their native status icons, with separate selected-character controls; player only sees owned character data.

Test Steps: 1) In a disposable world, GM opens Utilities > Party Inventory. 2) Click Create GM-only Party Stash. 3) Open Native Stash Sheet; drag or add `AG TEST | Sealed Travel Ledger` into its Items. 4) Return to Utilities.
Expected Outcome: Native GM-owned NPC stash and test Item/quantity appear in GM preview; no deposit/withdraw control exists.

Test Steps: 1) With Player Access enabled, Player 1 opens Utilities. 2) GM Utilities > GM Setup disables Player Access and saves. 3) Player 1 opens Console (F12) and runs `await game.modules.get('ashen-gate-utilities').api.open().then(() => 'UNEXPECTED OPEN', e => e.message)`.
Expected Outcome: Open player window closes; launcher disappears; console returns access denied; no Actor or Item state changes.

Test Steps: 1) Open Utilities; shrink window toward 620px wide and 490px tall. 2) Inspect tabs, Group Checks, Conditions panes, long names, control focus and buttons. 3) Expand window again.
Expected Outcome: Window enforces a practical minimum size and content remains readable, compact, keyboard-accessible, and unclipped.

Test Steps: 1) Connect two GM clients and Player 1 in disposable world. 2) Start a two-participant Group Check. 3) Player 1 rolls, disconnect the currently coordinating GM, then Player 1/2 makes a new roll. 4) Inspect progress and History.
Expected Outcome: One connected GM authoritatively accepts each roll once; no loss/duplicate on handover. Mark BLOCKED until two GM accounts are available.
